title: Your working setup
purpose: Understanding whose work these answers describe helps us avoid designing around the wrong kind of business.

questions.title: Whose work will your answers describe?
How many working vehicles does that work involve?
Which transportation services do you provide?
questions.help: Choose all that apply.

questions.title: Are those vehicles owned, leased, or a combination?
options: both|A combination of owned and leased

questions.title: What medallion arrangement applies to that work?
options: both|A combination of owned and leased medallions

questions.title: Do you work through a taxi association or co-op?
Who can accept a booking and commit the driver and vehicle?
How long is your current medallion lease?
questions.help: For example, six months, a year, or an ongoing arrangement. An estimate is fine. If you lease more than one medallion, focus on the main arrangement for both questions.

questions.title: How many consecutive medallion leases have you held, including your current lease?
questions.help: Use the same medallion arrangement as above. An estimate or "Not tracked / not sure" is fine.

questions.title: Which kinds of bookings do you actually fulfill?
questions.help: Choose all that apply. These can overlap: a scheduled pickup may also reserve a private vehicle.
options: private|An exclusive vehicle for one party

questions.title: Which pickup locations can you serve, and under what arrangements?
questions.help: For example, prearranged airport or ferry pickups, walk-up queues, hotel pickups, or drop-offs only. Mention any association or access conditions you work under, or what you are unsure about. Do not send permits or documents; this is discovery, not legal clearance.

title: How guests reach you
purpose: Knowing how guests find and contact you helps us distinguish a need for more visibility from a need for easier booking.

questions.title: How do new guests usually discover your business?
questions.help: Choose up to three. Think about how they find you, not how they send their message.

questions.title: How do booking inquiries usually reach you?
questions.help: Choose all that apply.

questions.title: Think of a recent booking: how did it go from the first inquiry to a confirmed arrangement?
questions.help: A brief account is enough, including what worked well. Please leave out guest names and contact details.

title: What you already use
purpose: We want to understand what existing options get right, where they fall short, and why some operators choose not to use them.
note: Think of websites, listings, booking apps, marketing services or dispatch networks that help bring in or arrange work. They do not have to be paid services. If you use several, focus on one for now.

questions.title: Have you joined or used any of these services?
options: current_recent|I use one now, including within the last 30 days
current_notrecent|I use one now, but have not used it in the last 30 days
former_recent|I stopped, but used it within the last 30 days
former|I used one before, but not within the last 30 days
considered|I considered one but never joined
never|I have not considered joining one

questions.title: Which service would you like to tell us about?
questions.help: The name is optional. Please focus on the same service in the next section.

questions.title: What mainly led you to join it?
What mainly kept you from joining?
What has made your current approach sufficient so far, or left you unsure about other options?
What makes it worth continuing to use?
questions.help: If it has not proved useful yet, that is helpful to know too.

questions.title: What made you stop using it?

title: What it costs and brings back
purpose: Understanding both the cost and the return helps us judge what would make a different service worthwhile, not simply add another expense.
skipNote: Based on your earlier answer, there is no current or recently used service to describe here. Continue to the next section, or go back if you would like to change that answer.
note: All figures are optional. Use the same service and the last 30 days throughout. Estimates are welcome. These figures describe associated work, not proof that the service created every booking.

questions.title: How does that service charge you?
questions.help: Choose all that apply. Choose "It is free" or "Not sure" on its own.

questions.title: Over the last 30 days, about how much did you pay that service?
questions.help: USD. Include fees deducted before payment reached you. Enter 0 if no payment fell in this period; annual or bundled charges may make that different from the ongoing cost.

questions.title: About how many completed bookings came through that service in those 30 days?
questions.help: Count bookings, not individual passengers. Choose "Not tracked / not sure" if you cannot estimate.

questions.title: About how much guest payment did those bookings bring in, before costs and service deductions?
questions.help: USD. Exclude money belonging to other operators. This is not a profit figure.

title: The work around the driving
purpose: A booking service should reduce unnecessary work, not give you another system to look after.

questions.title: Who normally handles booking inquiries while you are driving?
questions.help: Choose all that apply.
options: wait|Inquiries wait until I am available

questions.title: Which non-driving tasks take the most effort?
questions.help: Choose up to three. Choose "Nothing takes much effort" on its own.

questions.title: On a typical working day, how much of your own time goes into those tasks?
What do you use to keep arrangements organized?
questions.help: Choose all that apply.

questions.title: When you confirm a booking to a guest, what is already committed?
options: driver_vehicle|A particular driver and suitable vehicle
driver|A driver, with the vehicle still to be assigned
later|The driver and vehicle are arranged later

questions.title: How do you keep availability accurate when bookings arrive through different channels?
questions.help: For example, calls, WhatsApp, an association, or another booking service. What gets updated, and by whom? A brief description of your current process is enough.

questions.title: Who handles things when a pickup or booking goes wrong?
questions.help: For example, finding a replacement driver, updating the guest, handling a no-show or complaint, or arranging a refund. Describe what happens now, not what you think ETA should promise.

title: Work you could take
purpose: We need to distinguish opportunities a better process could recover from work you could not, or would not, want to take.

questions.title: In the last 30 days, about how many suitable inquiries failed to become completed work?
questions.help: Think of jobs you wanted and could reasonably have served, not work you deliberately chose to decline.

questions.title: What mainly prevented those jobs from going ahead?
questions.help: Choose up to three.

questions.title: What limits your ability to take additional work you would want?
questions.help: Choose up to three. Choose "Nothing" on its own.

questions.title: When, if ever, would additional work be useful?
questions.help: A brief description is enough. "I do not want additional work" is a useful answer too.

title: What remains after expenses
purpose: We want to understand what work brings in, where money already goes, and which expenses a different approach could replace or make more productive.
note: Use the same person, vehicle or business you described at the start, and the last 30 days. All figures are optional; estimates are welcome. Receipts minus reported expenses is a rough cash-flow return, not verified net profit. Annual bills, one-time costs and unpaid work can make that figure unrepresentative. Please do not send financial records or documents.

questions.title: Were the last 30 days quiet, typical or busy for your business?
About how many bookings did you complete in those 30 days?
questions.help: Use the same reporting scope as your other figures. Count completed bookings, not inquiries, cancellations, or individual passengers. An estimate or "Not tracked / not sure" is fine.

questions.title: How was that completed work split by booking type?
questions.help: For example: local rides, airport or ferry transfers, tours, stays, or events. Give approximate counts where you can. For per-person services, include paying passenger numbers; for vehicle-priced services, include vehicle bookings. Distinguish shared seats from private vehicles, and do not count the same booking twice. No price list is needed.

questions.title: Approximately how much did you collect for that work during those 30 days, before business costs or booking-service deductions?
questions.help: USD. Actual collections help us check any later revenue model. Exclude money belonging to other operators. Include service deductions when estimating the amount before costs.

questions.title: Approximately how much did you pay in business expenses during those 30 days?
questions.help: USD. Include service costs already reported; do not add them a second time. Exclude money simply passed to other operators. Annual or unusually large payments may make this period unrepresentative.

questions.title: What do you pay for, how much, and how often?
questions.help: List expenses separately: what each payment covers, the approximate amount, and its frequency (for example, weekly, monthly, annually, per trip, or one-time). Include whom you pay only if useful; no account details or private names. Consider fuel, maintenance, vehicle or medallion leases, insurance, permits or access, dispatch/booking services, marketing, financing, and paid administrative help. Identify costs shared with other work. Include previously reported service fees here for context, but count them only once in the 30-day total. Your own unpaid administrative time is recorded separately.

title: What would make a difference
purpose: Your priorities help us choose what deserves building, and what must not be disrupted.

questions.title: Which improvement would make the biggest practical difference to your business?
What must a different approach preserve for you?
questions.help: Choose up to three. Choose "Not sure" on its own.

questions.title: Which booking arrangement, if any, would be useful to you?
options: private|Tools for my own bookings only
overflow|Sharing work only when I choose

questions.title: Which existing task or expense would a different system need to replace or make more worthwhile?
questions.help: Name a current task, payment, or duplicated effort. What would need to stop, cost less, or produce a better result? We want to understand how existing spending could work better, not assume you want another bill.

questions.title: What have we misunderstood or not asked?
questions.help: Include anything important about your work or local arrangements that our questions missed.
